tests.title: A page carries next_cursor and has_more, and the cursor returns the following rows
given: an ordered set of 7 rows behind the pagination facility
tests.when: the first page of 3 is read and its next_cursor passed back twice more
then: the first two pages carry has_more true and a non-null next_cursor
the third carries has_more false and next_cursor null
the first row of each later page follows the previous page's last row
tests.pseudocode: in the pagination test file: p1 = page(limit=3); p2 = page(cursor=p1.next_cursor); p3 = page(cursor=p2.next_cursor); assert p3.next_cursor is None and rows(p1)+rows(p2)+rows(p3) == all_rows

tests.title: Reading every page of any set in any page size yields each row once in order
given: the pagination facility over generated sets of rows
tests.when: for generated row counts from 0 to 200, page sizes from 1 to 50 and both orders, pages are read until has_more is false
then: the concatenation equals the full set in the requested order
no row appears twice and none is missing
tests.pseudocode: in the pagination test file, a generative test over (rowCount, pageSize, order) asserting the collected rows

tests.title: A cursor this service did not issue is refused
given: one valid cursor and a set of bad ones: truncated, one character altered, from an unrelated encoding, empty, and re-encoded by hand
tests.when: a page is requested with each
then: each bad cursor answers 400 and returns no rows
the valid cursor still works afterwards
tests.pseudocode: in the pagination test file, table over the bad cursors asserting 400 and no rows, then asserting the good one still pages

tests.title: A session is opened and a repeated id returns the same session
given: a workspace the caller may write
tests.when: a session is opened with a client-chosen id, and the same id is opened again
then: the first answers 201 with the session, its credential id and type, status active and a start time
the second answers 200 with the same session unchanged
only one session exists
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' integration test file: a = post(sessions, {id}); b = post(sessions, {id}); assert a.status == 201 and b.status == 200 and count() == 1

tests.title: Opening a session needs write access whatever the workspace's status
given: an active and an archived workspace, their owner, a member of the organization, a stranger and an admin token
tests.when: each opens a session against each workspace
then: the owner and the admin token succeed against both
the member is refused
the stranger is refused
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file, table over (caller, workspaceStatus, expected)

tests.title: An open without a workspace, or for one the caller cannot see, is refused
given: a workspace the caller cannot see holding a session
tests.when: opens are made with no workspace_slug, an empty one, a slug naming nothing, a slug the caller cannot see, and replaying an id of the invisible workspace's session
then: the missing and empty slug answer 400
the other three answer 404 workspace not found
no session is recorded in any case
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file, table over the five cases asserting status and the session count

tests.title: A session is completed and its usage recorded
given: an active session opened by a known credential
tests.when: usage is reported twice for two models, the session is completed, and it is completed again
then: each usage report answers 201 with the record
the complete answers 200 with the session at the given status
the second complete answers 200 with the session unchanged
the session's token summary includes both reports
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' integration test file: post(usage); post(usage); r = post(complete); assert r.json.status == 'completed'; assert post(complete).json == r.json

tests.title: Only the session's creator or an admin token may close it or spend against it
given: a session opened by one credential, the workspace's owner who is not that credential, a second agent, and an admin token
tests.when: each calls the complete and the usage route for that session
then: the creator and the admin token are admitted
the workspace's owner, when not the creator, is refused
the second agent is refused
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file, table over (caller, route, expected)

tests.title: A bad complete is refused and the session unchanged
given: an active session, a terminal one, and a close already in flight
tests.when: completes are made with an unknown status, with terminated, by a caller who is not the creator, for a session that does not exist, and concurrently with another close
then: the unknown status and terminated answer 400
the wrong caller answers 403 not session owner
the unknown session answers 404
the concurrent close answers 409
the session's status is unchanged in every refusal
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file, table over the five cases asserting status and the stored session

tests.title: A bad usage report is refused and nothing recorded
given: an active session, a completed one, and a session of another creator
tests.when: usage is reported with no model, by a caller who is not the creator, for a session that does not exist, for the completed session, and with a negative token count
then: the missing model answers 400
the wrong caller answers 403
the unknown session answers 404
the completed session answers 409
the negative count answers 422
no usage record is written in any case
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file, table over the five cases asserting status and the usage count

tests.title: Sessions are listed with their filters, order and page size
given: sessions across two workspaces, two runs, several statuses, two credential types and two days
tests.when: the list is read with no filter, with each filter in turn, in both orders, and with page sizes of 1, 50 and 501
then: the default order is newest first and the default page size 50
each filter narrows the result to the matching sessions
a page size above 500 is capped at 500
each session carries its token summary
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' integration test file, table over the filters asserting the returned ids

tests.title: Usage totals cover the whole session whatever the page size
given: a session with 12 usage records across two models
tests.when: the usage is listed with page sizes of 1, 5 and 1000, and with a page size above 1000
then: the totals are identical in every case and cover all 12 records
the records paginate correctly
a page size above 1000 is capped at 1000
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' integration test file: assert {page(limit=n).totals for n in (1,5,1000)} has one element

tests.title: Session reads need read access and an active workspace
given: an active and an archived workspace, each with a session, and the owner, a member, a stranger and an admin token
tests.when: each reads the session list, the session and its usage for each workspace
then: the owner, the member and the admin token are served for the active workspace
every caller, the owner included, is answered 403 workspace access denied for the archived one
the stranger is answered 403 for the active one
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file, table over (caller, workspaceStatus, route, expected)

tests.title: An unknown session and an invalid cursor are refused
given: a session id naming nothing and an invalid cursor
tests.when: the session is read and the list and usage routes are called with the cursor
then: the unknown session answers 404
each invalid cursor answers 400
tests.pseudocode: in the session routes' test file: assert get(session, unknown).status == 404 and get(sessions, cursor=bad).status == 400

tests.title: Cost is aggregated by day, session and model and agrees with the sessions
given: three sessions across two days using two models, each with usage records
tests.when: the cost is read with no parameters and then grouped by day, by session and by model
then: the default grouping is day and the default period the last 24 hours
the totals equal the sum of the breakdown in every grouping
the totals agree with the sum of the sessions' own usage records
tests.pseudocode: in the cost integration test file, table over the groupings asserting sum(breakdown) == totals == sum(usage_records)

tests.title: An invalid period or grouping is refused
given: a workspace with sessions
tests.when: the cost is read with a start equal to the end, a start after the end, and a grouping of hour and of an empty string
then: each answers 400 in the error envelope
tests.pseudocode: in the cost test file, table over the four cases asserting 400

tests.title: Cost reads are refused for an archived or unreadable workspace
given: an archived workspace and one the caller cannot read
tests.when: the cost is read by the owner, a member, a stranger and an admin token
then: every caller is answered 403 workspace access denied for the archived workspace
the stranger is answered 403 for the readable one
tests.pseudocode: in the cost test file, table over (caller, workspaceStatus) asserting 403

tests.title: Archiving or deleting a workspace ends its active sessions
given: a workspace with two active sessions and one already completed, and a second workspace with one active session
tests.when: the first workspace is archived and the second's is deleted after archiving
then: each formerly active session has status terminated afterwards
the already completed session is unchanged
no session of either workspace remains active
sessions of other workspaces are untouched
tests.pseudocode: in the session lifecycle integration test file: post(archive); assert statuses(sessions(ws)) == ['terminated','terminated','completed']

tests.title: An agent run is recorded end to end against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a workspace the caller may write
tests.when: a session is opened, usage is reported twice for two models, the session is completed, and the session and its usage are read back
then: the open answers 201 and the complete 200
the session's token summary covers both reports
the usage list's totals cover both records whatever the page size
tests.pseudocode: in the sessions smoke test file: s = post(sessions); post(usage); post(usage); post(complete); assert totals(get(usage)) == expected

tests.title: A cost report is read across days and models against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and several recorded sessions across two days and two models
tests.when: the workspace's cost is read grouped by day and then by model
then: both answer 200 with totals and a breakdown
the two groupings report the same totals
the totals agree with the sessions' usage records
tests.pseudocode: in the cost smoke test file: d = get(cost, group_by='day'); m = get(cost, group_by='model'); assert d.json.totals == m.json.totals

tests.title: Archiving a workspace terminates its running session
given: a running deployment, a workspace and an open session against it
tests.when: the workspace is archived and the session is then read
then: the session's status is terminated
the read of the session is answered 403 workspace access denied
no session of the workspace remains active
tests.pseudocode: in the sessions smoke test file: post(archive); assert get(session).status == 403 and status_via_admin(session) == 'terminated'
